citation.authors: Revheim I, Ballance S, Standal AF et al.
citation.title: The acute effect of a β-glucan-enriched oat bread on gastric emptying, GLP-1 response, and postprandial glycaemia and insulinemia: a randomised crossover trial in healthy adults

population.description: 22 healthy adults (8 men, 14 women) who completed the crossover trial; enrolment 18-40 y, BMI 18.5-30 kg/m2, fasting glucose <= 7 mmol/L and HbA1c <= 48 mmol/mol (Table 2: age 24.6 ± 3.1 y, BMI 23.1 ± 2.7 kg/m2, mean ± SD).

protocols.name: oat_bread
protocols.description: Visit at 8:15 a.m. after an overnight fast; beta-glucan-enriched oat bread (94.1 g) with 250 mL water, eaten within 10 min (mean 7.1 min), standardised to 25 g available carbohydrate (Table 1: fat 2.9 g, protein 7.6 g, total fibre 5.5 g, sugar 1.1 g, total beta-glucan 3.6 g); blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min after the start of eating. The paper says the study breads contain gluten proteins (Discussion), so protein_source is 'plant'. Fat types not printed. start_hour taken as the 8:15 visit time (meal start not stated); prefast_hours not stated.

meals.food: beta-glucan-enriched oat bread, 94.1 g, with 250 mL water

protocols.name: wheat_bread
protocols.description: The same visit with whole-wheat bread (60.1 g) with 250 mL water, standardised to 25 g available carbohydrate (Table 1: fat 3.1 g, protein 4.1 g, total fibre 2.4 g, sugar 1.6 g, total beta-glucan 0.2 g); blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min. The paper says the study breads contain gluten proteins (Discussion), so protein_source is 'plant'. Fat types not printed. start_hour taken as the 8:15 visit time (meal start not stated); prefast_hours not stated.

meals.food: whole-wheat bread, 60.1 g, with 250 mL water

findings.description: Fasting serum insulin of all 22 participants, mean ± SD (Table 2, Total column). The table prints the unit as 'mlU/L', read as mIU/L (the Results print 'mLU/L' and 'mlU/L' for the same quantity; the levels, 5.2 fasting and 21 to 32 at the peak, fit mIU/L). Table 2 does not say at which visit or minute the sample was drawn; Methods define baseline as the fasting state at t = 0 min.

left_out.what: Capillary blood glucose levels: Cmax (Results) and fasting (Table 2, Total column). The paper's Table 2 footnote puts its capillary values on a whole-blood scale (plasma glucose divided by 1.11), about 10% below the plasma glucose the model carries; only Tmax, a time, is entered

Glucose iAUC2h (38.9 (22.9, 66.1) vs 87.1 (65.4, 115.9) mmol/L*min) and GLP-1 iAUC2h (139 (72, 268) vs 50 (17, 151) pM*min): printed as geometric means with 95% CI after log-transformation, but both are incremental areas (baseline-subtracted per person), not a geometric area of the marker (geometric_area is for the marker's own trapezoid area); the glucose values are also capillary whole-blood
GLP-1 time course (Fig. 3) and glucose and insulin curves (Fig. 4): the curve values are in the figures only
Gastric emptying by antrum ultrasound: T1/2, Tlag, rate constant k and peak antrum cross-sectional area (Results, Gastric emptying)
Differences between breads (p-values and the mixed-model treatment effect): no between-bread difference with its own uncertainty is printed
Systolic BP 111.1 ± 65.1 mmHg (Table 2): the SD is implausible beside the sex columns (13.5 and 5.5); not entered
HbA1c, 30.2 mmol/mol (Table 2, total and by sex)
